verdict.rationale: Sill's own docs say it has no account and no server, so session traffic travels only between the user's own devices. Remote use away from home goes through the admin's own VPN (e.g. Tailscale) or a port forwarded on their own router, so there is no vendor rendezvous or relay to replace. Missing for 10: no first-party self-hostable relay/rendezvous component for NAT traversal without your own VPN or port forwarding, no detail on network paths or the encryption protocol, no independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can self-host the rendezvous or relay infrastructure so session traffic stays on infrastructure I run

citations.quote: There is no account and no server: your screen and what you type travel only between your own devices
Remote Access lets you use your Mac away from home, through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, or through a port you forward on your router.
only the devices you paired can connect, and every connection is encrypted.
